quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, what is the best group formation?
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is good for normal riding, but use single-file formation when going through curves, making turns, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you do to adjust for the added weight?

options.text: Operate at a slower speed than usual.
Maintain a shorter following distance than you would without a passenger.
Operate at a faster speed than usual.
Brake a little later than you would without a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Operate at a slower speed than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing down earlier, increase your following distance, and look for larger gaps when crossing or merging with traffic.

questions.question: When entering a turn, what should a rider do?

options.text: Move their shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by closing the throttle and using both brakes if needed.

questions.question: Which step is NOT safe for preventing fatigue while riding?

options.text: Limiting the distance ridden in one day

questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks and avoid riding more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Do not use artificial stimulants—they become dangerous when their effects wear off.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your lane position as road and traffic conditions change. Choose a position that gives you the most space around you and makes it easier for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: Riders who do not wear helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders who do wear helmets.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen frequently, so there is no need to worry about them.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be deadly.

questions.question: To increase your chances of being seen at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride as closely as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: The best way to be seen at an intersection is to keep your headlight on. Always ride with your headlight on whenever your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
Travel at a faster speed than usual to get to your destination more quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Decrease your following distance so you can be as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Be flexible with your lane position, especially at night. Always use safe riding strategies when conditions are poor.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when turning, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip opposite to the direction you are turning.
Press the handgrip in the direction you are turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you are turning.
questions.explanation: To turn, a motorcycle must lean. Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn to make the motorcycle lean.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear clothing and gear that makes you and your motorcycle easier to spot. Bright, reflective clothing helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because:

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. They could move into your lane without warning. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors, you should practice using them because:

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It is hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view of the road behind you. However, they make objects seem farther away than they actually are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has convex mirrors.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, they should:

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders passing at the same time.

questions.explanation: When a group of motorcycle riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. Wait until the first rider completes their pass before the next rider begins.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is located at the right handgrip and is controlled with the right hand.

questions.question: What should you do to stay in control while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To maintain control through a turn, look ahead through the turn by turning only your head. Slow down before turning and lean your motorcycle in the correct direction.

questions.question: Of crashes between a motorcycle and a car, how many are caused by the driver not properly yielding right-of-way?
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes between a motorcycle and a car happen because the driver did not properly yield right-of-way to the motorcycle rider.

questions.question: Engine braking is:

options.text: Slowing down by turning the engine off.
Not recommended because it damages the engine.

questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle, similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Rain suits:

options.text: Should not puff up when riding.
Are not needed because motorcycles should not be ridden in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not puff up when riding.
questions.explanation: Good quality rain suits made for motorcycles will not tear or puff up when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: You should keep more space between you and other vehicles when:

options.text: The road is wet or icy.
The temperature is colder than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is wet or icy.
questions.explanation: A two-second gap is normal following distance. Increase this gap when conditions make stopping harder, such as wet or icy roads.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Position yourself in the lane so other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
Always stay in the left lane to stay away from oncoming traffic.
Slowly ease up to the intersection.
Weave slightly in your lane so your headlight is more noticeable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself in the lane so other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Move to the part of your lane that lets oncoming drivers see you earliest. For example, at a blind right turn, move to the left side of your lane for better visibility.

questions.question: The best lane position is one that:

options.text: Allows you to draft off other vehicles.
Makes other drivers able to see you.
Places you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes other drivers able to see you.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed. Choose a position that gives you the most space.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of the lane?
questions.explanation: Oil drips from cars create a greasy strip in the center of lanes. In dry conditions, motorcycles can usually ride safely on this strip.

questions.question: Convex mirrors make cars appear:
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head. Press your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handlebars.

questions.question: What best protects your eyes from wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Most windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT need regular checking?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tires, controls, chain, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small mechanical problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous.

questions.question: The front brake provides what percentage of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It can supply at least 70 percent of the total stopping power.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in a staggered formation. However, switch to single-file when turning, going through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially hazardous because:

options.text: The front tire provides the power for the bike, so you will lose acceleration.
The flat tire will shake the bike, making it hard to use the mirrors.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because it affects your steering ability. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely leave the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can more easily see the lights of other vehicles.
More difficult than riding during the day because it is harder to see.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than riding during the day because it is harder to see.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because visibility is poor. Without normal shadows and light contrasts, it is harder to judge distances and be seen by other drivers.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following, except:

options.text: How much tread is on your tires.
The general condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire air pressure, tire tread wear, and the general condition of the tire sidewalls and tread surface.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is considered legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Normally, you should maintain a following distance of:
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: When someone follows you too closely, you should:

options.text: Not worry about them and just focus on the road in front of you.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate at a higher speed, increasing danger. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers do not expect you there.

questions.question: Alcohol impairment:

options.text: Begins at about half of the legal limit.
Occurs only if you have had multiple drinks.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can impair your riding ability. You can be impaired below the legal limit. No amount of alcohol is safe before riding.

questions.question: You should choose the lane position that can:

options.text: Minimize your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
Maximize your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
Maximize your potential for encountering road hazards and allow others to pass you.
Minimize your potential for encountering road hazards and allow you to closely follow another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maximize your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
questions.explanation: The right lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It discourages others from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route. Choose a position that maximizes your space cushion.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is not dangerous. Simply relax and go straight at a steady speed. Trying to weave to match the movement will make things more dangerous.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, what should you think about?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead of you.
Which position makes your trip shorter.
If you can pass more vehicles in one position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position so other drivers can see you. You also need enough space around you to react to problems.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night. This makes other drivers more likely to see you.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good way to be more visible to other drivers?

options.text: Using your headlight at all times

questions.explanation: To be visible, wear bright or reflective clothing, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light correctly. Waving does not help other drivers see you.

questions.question: A friend has drunk too much and wants to ride their motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has drunk too much to ride. Take their keys if needed and help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about dangers ahead.

questions.question: Your lane position should help you:

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
Stay in other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: A good lane position protects your space and shows other drivers what you intend to do.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You can finish the pass in a no passing zone.
You can go 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
You must pass on the shoulder if one is available.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: Passing must happen only in areas where it is safe and legal. Stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: When a group of riders gets on a highway, they should form:
questions.explanation: While a staggered line works best on normal roads, groups should use a single line when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Your motorcycle starts to wobble. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up—this makes wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed by closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and low. Pull over as soon as safely possible. Avoid braking suddenly, as this can worsen the wobble.
